source.title: Exploring the coherence of features explanations in the GemmaScope

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates heuristic relevance of GemmaScope SAE feature explanations to the inputs that activate them. It does not test neuron-pole job counts, held-out prediction of neuron activations, or explanation scores from simulated activations on new text as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports a distribution of heuristic coherence categories for the five strongest SAE features per target word. These results concern a related explanation-coherence question, but do not measure any claim version as stated. Background claims and examples cited from other work are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study scores GemmaScope SAE-feature explanations (Gemma-2b, layer 25 residual stream) for relevance to animal-word inputs using keyword heuristics. SAE features are not the model's own neurons, and it reports no neuron-pole shares, simulation scores or held-out activation prediction. It bears on no version as stated; the finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that, at Gemma-2b's layer-25 post-MLP residual SAE, explanations of the top-5 activating features for their animal inputs are largely incoherent with those inputs. They stress that the work is exploratory and that the heuristic is crude and may miss synonyms.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a single Gemma-2b SAE location and heuristic keyword/pattern matching to assess explanation relevance to activating inputs; it does not audit neuron poles or test the claim's neuron-based method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study tests only the post-MLP residual stream at layer 25 and separates results by top-5 activation rank; it does not compare locations or models.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2b, for 111 'The X is a Y' animal sentences, most GemmaScope explanations of the top-5 SAE features firing on the animal token were judged unrelated to it (80–98 of 111 per rank). The top2 rank had more animal-related explanations (29) than top1 (12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-generated explanations of the SAE features that fire most strongly on a given input often do not match that input, by a simple keyword heuristic.

record.problems: The authors identify the heuristic as simple and potentially liable to miss coherent explanations such as synonyms. The analysis covers one model, one SAE location, and 111 single-token animal words in a fixed sentence template; it does not test other contexts or locations. No uncertainty estimates or controls are reported.

untested.parts: Neuron-pole shares across models and scale
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and the pose reading
Architecture and tool effects on the share of interpretable neurons
Neuron-based attribution graphs versus replacement models
Whether neuron explanations from activating examples predict firing elsewhere. The study looks only at SAE features, not neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The study's units are SAE features, not neurons, and the explanations come from Neuronpedia/GemmaScope rather than the authors' own scoring. The design runs from input to explanation rather than from explanation to prediction. It therefore resembles V6 in spirit but does not measure any version. The heuristic has no controls and no uncertainty estimates, and covers one SAE location and 111 animal words in a single sentence template.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole job shares across models, architectures, and scales.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and the proposed pose explanation.
Architecture, regularization, tool quality, and the stated interpretability estimates for InceptionV1-sized models.
Attribution graphs using a large model's own neurons and comparison with a trained replacement model.
Whether explanations that fit activating examples predict activation on other examples.
Automated explanation scores based on simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: Gemma-2b
rows.operation_detail: Heuristic pattern matching categorized explanations for the top-5 activating SAE features.
rows.measure: Counts of explanations in heuristic categories 0–4, respectively: unrelated; animal-related; target hypernym; target concept; mention of target word.
rows.note: The five counts are read in the table's stated category order; they sum to 111.
rows.check: Value misread from the flattened Table 1 string 'Top19812010'. The text says top1 has 12 animal-related explanations ('top2 (29) instead of the top1 (12)'). The correct counts are 98, 12, 0, 1, 0, not 98, 1, 2, 0, 10. Both sum to 111.
